name: Kritisch-Watten
description: Kritisch-Watten (also known as Bayerisch Watten or Kritisch Warp) is a popular Alpine variant of the trick-taking game Watten, widely played in Bavaria, Tyrol (Austria), and South Tyrol. It is distinguished by the presence of 'Kritische Karten' (Criticals or Kritten)â€”permanent trumps that rank above all other cards, including the elected trump suit and rank. history.origins: Watten dates back to the early 19th Century, allegedly popularized by soldiers during the Napoleonic Wars. 'Kritisch-Watten' emerged as the more competitive variant in Alpine taverns.
timeline: 1850s: The 'Critical' card hierarchy standardizes in South Tyrol and Bavaria.
Present: A semi-official sport in many Tyrolean villages with high participation in local 'Preiswatten' (tournaments).
history.cultural: Signaling (Deuten) is a core cultural part of the game; partners communicate cards with subtle facial expressions (e.g., blinking or puffing cheeks).
history.evolution: The game evolved to include the 'Weli' (6 of Bells) as a wildcard or critical card in many Austrian versions, increasing the complexity of the trump hierarchy.

setup.deck: 33 cards in Tyrol (including the 'Weli'). Hearts, Leaves, Acorns, Bells. Standard Ranks: Sau (Ace), K, O, U, 10, 9, 8, 7.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards (packets of 3 then 2).

rules.objective: Each partnership aims to win at least three of the five tricks in each hand; the team that does so scores points (typically two unless the stake was raised), and the first team to reach 11 points wins the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Usually, there is NO obligation to follow suit or rank.
2. **Exception (Trump Lead)**: If the 'Haube' (the principal trump) is led, others MUST play a trump if they have one.
keyRules: The three Criticals (Kritische Karten) are permanent trumps: King of Hearts (Maxl), Seven of Bells (Belli), Seven of Acorns (Spitz)
Forehand chooses the Schlag (rank), dealer chooses the Farbe (suit)
No obligation to follow suit except when the Haube is led
Players can 'offer' to raise the stake during play

strategy.basic: Identify the 'Machine': If you or your partner holds all three Criticals, you have an unbreakable hand. Signal your partner immediately to ensure they don't 'offer' a raise until you are ready.
strategy.intermediate: The Signaling (Deuten): Use standard signals: Tongue to the side for the Maxl (KH), wink for the Belli (7B), and shoulder-shrug for the Spitz (7A). Coordination is key to winning without wasting high trumps on the same trick.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing the Raise: If you win the first two tricks and have nothing left, 'offer' to raise the points to 3. If the opponents haven't coordinated their signals well, they may fold, giving you the win despite a weak hand.
tips: The 'Haube' (the card matching BOTH suit and rank chosen) is the most powerful non-critical card. Use it to force trumps out of your opponents' hands.
In Tyrol, always check if the 'Weli' is being used as a critical or just a rank-filler; it changes the hierarchy significantly.
